Lead Story • Project Milestone

Vanguard Commissions 18-MW Harborview Transit & Hospital Microgrid Ahead of Schedule

By Elena Rostova, PE, Director of Power & Controls • November 23, 2026

Last Thursday at 04:00 EST, a 34-person multidisciplinary team spanning our Power Systems, Civil-Structural, and Embedded Controls groups completed live islanding verification for the Harborview Regional Resilience Microgrid. Under full simulated grid-loss conditions, the facility seamlessly transitioned both the Harborview Trauma Center and the Eastside Light-Rail Traction Substation onto local battery storage and combined heat-and-power generation in under 68 milliseconds.

18.4 MW Peak Islanded Capacity
67.4 ms Grid-to-Island Transfer Time
0 Recordable Safety Incidents (41,200 hrs)

Originally slated for turnover in mid-December, our field commissioning crew shaved three weeks off the critical path by building a hardware-in-the-loop digital twin in our Denver lab prior to switchgear delivery. That upfront simulation caught two relay coordination edge cases before a single cable was pulled on-site.

Special recognition goes to site lead Marcus Vance, structural foundation lead Priya Nair, and the entire protection-and-controls bench across our Boston, Denver, and Seattle offices. We will host a technical lessons-learned brown bag on December 4 to walk through the controller architecture and seismic anchorage details.

Employee Spotlight

Meet Tomás Herrera, SE — Senior Bridge & Seismic Engineer

TH
Tomás Herrera, SE
Structural Practice
Seattle Office
6 Years at Vanguard

If you have ever used Vanguard's automated nonlinear pushover scripts in OpenSees—or tasted the legendary smoked brisket at the Seattle summer picnic—you already know Tomás Herrera. Since joining our 45-person Seattle studio in 2020, Tomás has led seismic retrofit designs for nine lifeline bridges and mentored a dozen junior engineers through their SE lateral exams.

“What keeps me energized in a 200-person firm is the sweet spot of scale: we tackle infrastructure problems big enough to matter to an entire city, yet I can walk twenty feet down the hall and whiteboard a soil-structure interaction puzzle with the geotech lead in ten minutes.”

Current obsession at work: Developing parametric base-isolation connection details for the Alder Creek Steel Arch Replacement.
Outside the office: Restoring a 1978 steel-frame touring bicycle, sea kayaking around Puget Sound, and coaching his daughter's U-10 soccer squad.
Ask him about: Post-tensioned rocking bridge piers, cast-iron sourdough baking, or his favorite rainy-day Espresso spots in Pioneer Square.
